root_cause.text: The ublk driver deferred resetting the per-IO canceled flag (UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED) until all IOs in a queue were fetched, causing a deadlock when only a subset were fetched before the server died, as the remaining canceled flag prevented cancellation completion.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "the per-IO canceled flags for all IOs in a queue are reset together only once all IOs for that queue have been fetched. So if a nonempty proper subset of the IOs for a queue are fetched when the ublk server dies, the IOs in that subset will never successfully be canceled, as their canceled flags remain set." The patch moves the flag reset from the batch function `ublk_queue_reset_io_flags` to a new per-IO function `ublk_reset_io_flags` called on each individual fetch in `ublk_mark_io_ready`.

candidates.rationale: This statement resets the canceled flag for each IO, but it is only called when all IOs are fetched, causing a deadlock if only a subset were fetched before server failure.
Setting canceling to false is part of the deferred reset; if not done in time, the cancel state persists and prevents completion.
The lock taken during the deferred reset contributes to the deadlock if the cancel path is blocked before this point.
Release of the lock also part of the deferred reset; deadlock occurs if this lock is held or not released in time.
Resetting fail_io is also done only when all IOs are fetched, contributing to the incorrect state if not reset.
This per-IO marking does not clear the canceled flag; the reset is deferred until all are ready, so the cancel flag remains for the remaining IOs.
Similar to above, marking IO ready does not reset the canceled flag, causing the deadlock when not all IOs are fetched.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement resets the UBLK_IO_FLAG_CANCELED flag per IO, but it is only executed when all IOs in the queue are fetched (deferred). If only a subset of IOs are fetched before the server dies, the remaining IOs keep the flag set, preventing cancellation completion and causing a deadlock.

This lock is acquired before resetting the canceled flag and other state variables. Because the reset is deferred until all IOs are fetched, this lock can be held or blocked, contributing to the deadlock if cancellation path requires this lock or waits for the flag to be cleared.
Setting 'canceling' to false is part of the deferred reset. If all IOs are not fetched, 'canceling' remains true, which can block completion and contribute to the deadlock.
Release of the cancel_lock also occurs only after all IOs are fetched. If the lock is not released in time due to the deferred reset, it can lead to a deadlock when other paths try to acquire it.
Resetting 'fail_io' is also deferred until all IOs are fetched. Incorrect state persists if not all IOs are fetched, contributing to the inconsistent state that leads to deadlock.

This per-IO marking occurs during fetch but does not reset the per-IO canceled flag. The canceled flag is only cleared later in the deferred block, so if not all IOs are fetched, the flag remains set on remaining IOs, causing the deadlock.

Similar to the previous statement, this marks an IO as ready without clearing the canceled flag. The lack of per-IO flag reset here (deferred to later batch) leads to the deadlock when only a subset of IOs are fetched.
